content: Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of liposomal doxorubicin by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4. Dronabinol is a substrate of CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of dutasteride by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. The elagolix dose should be limited to 150 mg daily, and the duration of CYP3A inhibitor use should not exceed six months. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels of eluxadoline by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is advised when co-administered with strong CYP2C9/10 inhibitors. Ketoconazole and elvitegravir mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. If co-administered, ketoconazole should not exceed 200 mg/day, and no dose adjustment is needed for elvitegravir. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Ketoconazole should be limited to 200 mg/day when co-administered with this combination therapy. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Enfortumab vedotin releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), which is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Close monitoring for signs of toxicity is recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Similarly, ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Ketoconazole also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Ketoconazole also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Ketoconazole also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of estradiol by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations of estrogens and associated toxicities. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of eszopiclone by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The eszopiclone dose should not exceed 2 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole, may increase plasma hormone levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethosuximide by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethotoin by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of etoposide by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of etravirine by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 and by affecting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Ketoconazole, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and substrate, may increase plasma concentrations of etravirine, while etravirine may decrease ketoconazole plasma concentrations. Dose adjustments of ketoconazole may be necessary depending on co-administered drugs. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of eucalyptus by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of felbamate by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fentanyl by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Frequent monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation is necessary, and fentanyl dose adjustments should be considered until stable drug effects are achieved. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal) by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Frequent monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation is necessary, and fentanyl dose adjustments should be considered until stable drug effects are achieved. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of finasteride by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels of fingolimod by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic enzyme CYP4F2. Monitor for adverse events of fingolimod when used concomitantly with ketoconazole. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole and flecainide both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of inhaled flunisolide by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole and fluoxetine both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of flurazepam by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the toxicity of fluvastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole and fluvoxamine both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole and foscarnet both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fosphenytoin by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Monitor for toxicities that may require dose reduction. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels of gefitinib by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of adverse effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of gentamicin by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole and givinostat both increase the QTc interval. If co-administered, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide by decreasing their metabolism. Strong CYP2C9 inhibitors may also decrease glyburide metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Grapefruit decreases the levels of ketoconazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, the dosage should be reduced to half the recommended dose if co-administered. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, potentially decreasing its efficacy. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole and iloperidone both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels of inhaled indacaterol by modulating both P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 activities. No dose adjustment is warranted at the 75 mcg dose. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of irinotecan and liposomal irinotecan by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of istradefylline by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The istradefylline dose should not exceed 20 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The ivacaftor dose should be reduced when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product labeling for precise dosage modifications. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ivermectin by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels of lacosamide by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Dose reduction may be necessary in these patients. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ketoconazole and lapatinib both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lesinurad by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the effects of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Letermovir increases the levels of ketoconazole by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole and levofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The levomilnacipran dose should not exceed 80 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of oral levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. The use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of linagliptin by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of loperamide by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Ketoconazole doses greater than 200 mg/day are not recommended when used concurrently with lopinavir/ritonavir. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of losartan by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. This may inhibit the conversion of losartan to its active metabolite E-3174. The clinical significance of this interaction is not established; monitor individual therapeutic response to determine losartan dosage. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients already taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. Following this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The lumateperone dose should not exceed 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The maraviroc dose should be decreased to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of marijuana by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of mavorizxafor by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor mavorizxafor levels if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors, and reduce the mavorizxafor dose if needed. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of mestranol by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole and mipomersen both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Both drugs have the potential to elevate hepatic enzymes; monitor liver function tests (LFTs). Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Reduce the mirtazapine dose if co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary. Once the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the mirtazapine dose. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of modafinil by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of inhaled mometasone by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This increases the risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of intranasal mometasone by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of montelukast by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor naldemedine for potential adverse effects if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
